Then links to this: https://techcrunch.com/2017/12/20/apple-addresses-why-people-are-saying-their-iphones-with-older-batteries-are-running-slower/

Which clearly says:

Apple is focusing attention on smoothing out the very high and quick peaks of power draw that can cause problems with older batteries.

And then quotes Apple:

Lithium-ion batteries become less capable of supplying peak current demands when in cold conditions, have a low battery charge or as they age over time and we released a feature for iPhone 6, iPhone 6s and iPhone SE to smooth out the instantaneous peaks only when needed to prevent the device from unexpectedly shutting down

Which is then explained as:

As that battery ages, iOS will check its responsiveness and effectiveness actively. At a point when it becomes unable to give the processor all the power it needs to hit a peak of power, the requests will be spread out over a few cycles.

And summarized with:

This will not affect the average performance of your device, and it is emphatically not throttling; it’s capping the peak demands and not allowing them to be as high — and spreading that work out over more cycles rather than one.

So to be exact, Apple does not "throttles processor speeds", rather, they adjust cpu time scheduling to spread high cpu usage over longer period of time, which can result in less smooth user experience.
